epigrafe.descrizione: A complete Roman copper-alloy nummus of Constantine II dating from AD 322 to 324. CAESARVM NOSTRORVM reverse type depicting a wreath, which would have contained a vow (VOT X), indicating an anniversary. Obverse: [CONSTANTINVS IVN NOB C] / Helmeted and cuirassed bust right. Reverse: [CAESARVM NOSTRORVM] / Wreath enclosing inscription VOT X. Diameter: 18.20 mm; Thickness: 1.07 mm; Weight: 1.84g
epigrafe.fotografo: The Portable Antiquities Scheme, Simon Collins

epigrafe.descrizione: A complete and worn, copper-alloy Roman nummus of Crispus c.317-318 AD. Mint of Trier. Officina number A (Alpha). Reece Period 16. As RIC 7 no. 170. Obverse description: Laureate & draped bust facing right. Obverse inscription: FL.IVL.CRISPVS.NOB.CAES. Reverse description: Prince in military dress standing right holding transverse spear and globe. Reverse inscription: PRINCIPI IVVENTVTIS. Reverse mint mark: F T // ATR. Diameter: 19.69 mm; Thickness: 1.58 mm; Weight: 2.72g
epigrafe.fotografo: The Portable Antiquities Scheme, Simon Collins

epigrafe.descrizione: Roman silver denarius of Septimus Severus, 17mm in diameter, 2mm thick with a weight of 3grams. The obverse shows right facing bearded laureate bust with inscription [...]SEPTSEVPERT[...] The coin is missing part of its edge so some of the inscription is missing. Reverse shows left facing seated female with branch in right hand and staff in left. Inscription reads [...]ACIACTERNAE[...]

epigrafe.descrizione: A silver finger ring, Henig Type VIII, dating to the 2nd-3rd centuries AD. The ring has an oval bezel with the letters ToT inscribed in the centre. The letters 'T' are undecorative and formed by simple lines. The letter 'o' is shown in the lower case. There are two transversely incised lines above and below the inscription. There are no lines to the side however this may be due to wear rather…

epigrafe.descrizione: A Roman copper alloy barbarous radiate coin forgery, dating from AD275-285 (Reece Period 14). The reverse appears to depict a standing figure, possibly a soldier, with a short skirt. All that is visible of the inscription is AVG. This coin is possibly attempting to copy the VIRTVS AVG type. Dimensions: diameter: 11.73 mm; weight: 0.70g

epigrafe.provenienza: contea di ritrovamento: Cornwall (Inghilterra e Galles)
epigrafe.descrizione: Roman copper alloy sestertius, probably of Vespasian (AD 69-79), Reece period 4, possibly SALVS AVGVSTA S C reverse type depicting Salus seated left holding patera out in right hand and sceptre in left, but the coin is incomplete and broken in two places. The back of the portrait head is just visible, as are the letters [IM]P CAE[S...] in the obverse inscription which combined with the curvature of the thick neck and the shape of the head suggest Vespasian. The coin is quite large as even with areas of the circumference missing it measures 27 mm in diameter. Cf. RIC Vol. II, part 1, p.146, pl.65, no.1208

epigrafe.descrizione: A complete copper-alloy finger ring dating to the second or third centuries AD. The hoop is hemispherical in section and very worn suggesting use wear. It extends to slightly expanded shoulders. The bezel is oval in plan and is decorated with a stamped inscription within a lozengiform stamped border which reads 'AVE AMA' - 'Greetings. Love (me).' The inscriptions 'Ave' and 'Ama' are reasonably common on finger rings (see CIL xiii 10024.39ff for examples). At Ribchester, a gold ring with the inscription 'AVE MEA VITA' has been found (CIL vii 1306) and a further example with the inscription 'AVE ME' found at Carlisle (JRS Iiii (1963) 163, No. 23). It conforms to Guiraud's Type 2g (Guiraud…

Obverse description: Bust laureate draped and cuirassed right. Obverse inscription: FL IVL CRISPVS NOB CAES. Reverse description: Two Victories holding shield inscribed VOT / PR over altar with wreath on front. Reverse inscription: VICTORIAE LAETAE PRINC [PERP]. In exergue: PTR (CR reads PLN]. Cliff Reeves kindly identified this coin, citing RIC volume 7 pages 107-8, nos 164 and 174. Diameter: 18.8mm, Weight: 2.52gms, die axis: 6

epigrafe.descrizione: A probable modern copy of a copper alloy Roman radiate of Allectus dating to the period AD 293-96 (Reece Period 14). Reverse inscription: PROVIDENTIA AVG. Reverse image: Providentia standing left, holding a baton and a cornucopiae, globe at foot. Mint unclear - it migh be S P // (ML?) for London, but this type is very rare for London. It is more likely to be S P // (C) for C Mint which is much more common (cf RIC V, pt 2, p. 561, no. 35). The thickness and cast nature of the coin, indicate that this is a forgery and not contemporary to the Roman period. This coin has been included in the copies section of Sam Moorhead's corpus for RIC. Obverse: IMP C ALLECTVS P F AVG; Radiate and cuirassed…

epigrafe.descrizione: An incomplete Roman ceramic stamped amphora handle dating to the 2nd century AD. This handle is possible from a Dressel 20 amphora which would have been large and globular with cylindrical handles and a prominent beaded or angular rim. The fabric is buff coloured and granular. The handle is stamped with the remaining inscription which reads 'EVET'. A similar amphora on the database is LON-D190C6. Dimensions: length: 98.92mm; width: 49.13mm; weight: 243g. References: Callender, M. H. 1965. Roman Amphorae. Oxford University Press; Oxford. Funari, P. P. A. 1996. Dressel 20 inscriptions from Britain and the consumption of Spanish olive oil: with catalogue of stamps. Oxford: Tempus Reparatum

epigrafe.descrizione: Fragment of a Roman finger ring made of jet or shale. The hoop is thick, D-shaped in cross-section and only remains as part of one shoulder. The bezel is rectangular and very slightly raised from the hoop.The bezel is decorated with an incised rectangle with a hatched border. The interior of the rectangular, which usually carries an inscription, is blank. The design is one that is often seen in silver Roman finger rings of the second and third centuries that equate to Henig's type XI rings.. Jet jewellery was popular in the Roman period, and one of the main sources was the East coast of Yorkshire, so it is likely that this ring was made locally from material in the region. epigrafe.provenienza: contea di ritrovamento: Lincolnshire (Inghilterra e Galles)
epigrafe.descrizione: Copper alloy coin. Nummus of House of Constantine (306-361), irregular copy of a fallen horseman issue of 355-361, though of an unfamiliar variety, with the obverse emphasising imperial regalia, with a banded diadem and a mantle fastened at the shoulder. The face is rendered with unusual animation, though the appearance of a pimple on the end of an elongated nose may be fortuitous. Reece period 18. Obverse description: Bust draped and diademed right. Reverse description: Stick man soldier advancing left with spear arm raised; the horseman is off flan. Reverse inscription: [FEL TEMP REPARATIO]. Diameter: 13.4mm, Weight: 1.14gms, die axis: 12

epigrafe.descrizione: Copper alloy. Coin. Nummus fraction of House of Constantine (306-361) with deliberately sheared edge, cut in antiquity, probably a fallen horseman issue of 355-361, Reece period 18. Obverse description: Bust right. Reverse description: Probably soldier advancing left spearing fallen horseman; the horse's legs are the identifying trait. Reverse inscription: [FEL TE]MP [REPARATIO]. In exergue: TH, letters seriffed with pellets, possibly Thessalonica mint. Diameter: 16.5mm, Weight: 1.43gms, die axis: probably 6

epigrafe.testo: CONSTANTINVS IVN NOB C' (CONSTANTINE THE YOUNGER NOBLE CAESAR)
epigrafe.descrizione: A copper alloy Roman Nummus of Constantine II, dating from around 330-335 CE. Bust right of Constantine II which the inscription 'CONSTANTINVS IVN NOB C' (CONSTANTINE THE YOUNGER NOBLE CAESAR). On the opposite side of the coin it has an image of two Roman soldiers and two standards, with the minters mark 'PLG' (Lugdunum: Lyons, France). GLORIA EXERCITVS reverse type

epigrafe.testo: D/ DN CONSTAN TIVS PF AVG ; R/ FEL TEMP REPARATIO
epigrafe.descrizione: Copper alloy coin. Nummus of Constantius II (323-361), Fallen Horseman issue of 355-361, Reece period 18; Lyons mint, possibly RIC vol. 8 page 190 no. 183, issue of 353-355. Obverse description: Bust draped and cuirassed pearl diademed right, seen from front. Obverse inscription: DN CONSTAN TIVS PF AVG. Reverse description: Soldier advancing left spearing fallen horseman; horseman wears brimmed and pointed hat, vertically ribbed or striped garment also suggested. Reverse inscription: FEL TEMP REPARATIO. In exergue: FPLG. Diameter: 17.8mm, Weight: 1.93gms, die axis: 6
epigrafe.licenza_metadati: CC BY-SA 4.0 (schede del PAS su Wikimedia Commons)

epigrafe.descrizione: A scattered coin hoard [or hoards; if so, of broadly similar date] of later Roman copper alloy radiates ranging from good, more generally fair condition, including 60 objects recognised to date, discovered by two finders. Of these, four coins have already been recorded as: NLM-2B3557, NLM-2B41FC, NLM-2B4EB4 and NLM-2B5A2C [locations listed on this record as nos. 15-18]. Those which initially lent themselves to identification were commemorative issues in honour of Claudius II (268-270) and may point to a date of deposition c.270, Reece period 13. Though the group includes coins from the mints of Rome and Milan, many are probably irregular, though not barbarous. All the coins were…

epigrafe.descrizione: Copper alloy coin. Nummus of House of Constantine (306-361), Beata Tranquillitas issue of 321-323, Reece period 16. Pierced with a drilled hole of diameter 2.5mm at 6 O'clock obverse. This issue was preferred for piercing for inclusion in Anglo-Saxon grave groups, and an Anglo-Saxon brooch fragment is reported from the same location. Obverse description: Head probably laureate right. Reverse description: Globe on altar. Reverse inscription: [BEATA TRANQVILLITAS], continuous status of legend indeterminate. Diameter: 18.5mm, Weight: 1.98gms, die axis: 12

epigrafe.descrizione: Report for H M Coroner. Bottesford (addenda), Lincolnshire. Richard Abdy. 4 AR denarii to AD 207 - see NLM-ADD973, NLM-ADA762, NLM-C03203 and NLM-28BC26 - this coin (NLM-28CBD5) is the fifth, stray coin. Stray coin. Also handed in from the same finder was a base silver radiate of Philip II as Caesar (AD 244-7), however as this forms a very obvious outlier to the denarius hoard group it is recorded below as a stray find. For DECCIUS, probably as a peregrine name, see RIB 1805 (Carvoran). Reference: Mark Hassall, in Roman…

epigrafe.provenienza: contea di ritrovamento: Nottinghamshire (Inghilterra e Galles)
epigrafe.descrizione: Complete copper alloy large Roman spoon. The spoon has a straight square-sectioned handle with a decorative step between the handle and bowl. At the terminal the handle tapers slightly to a point and at the other end (just before the step) on the top edge of the handle there is a pattern (or an inscription in roman numerals) III XX III. The step is shaped into the profile of a fish with protruding lips and there is a small hole depicting the eye. The bowl of the spoon is ovoid with a slightly blunted leading edge. The spoon is in good condition and measures 154.8mm in length, 32.6mm in width, 13.04mm in thickness and weighs 13.6g. A similar example can be seen in Hattatt’s Ancient Brooches…
epigrafe.fotografo: West Yorkshire Archaeology Service, Anna Marshall
epigrafe.licenza_metadati: CC BY-SA 4.0 (schede del PAS su Wikimedia Commons)

epigrafe.testo: Poorly formed raised retrograde letters apparently read: NIIMNISTIVS,
epigrafe.descrizione: A copper alloy Roman seal matrix with a cast name in retrograde. The object is roughly rectangular and has been crudely cast with flaws and bubbles on its surface. In the centre of the side opposite the name is the stub of an iron attachment. The projecting letters are formed from thin strokes. The object may have been used for impressing a name into a soft substance, such as butter or clay. Roger Tomlin reports on the inscription: Poorly formed raised retrograde letters apparently read: NIIMNISTIVS, (Nemnistius) The letters except for S are formed by vertical and diagonal strokes indistinctly divided, making it difficult to distinguish between M, N and V. The termination ISTIVS seems clear…

epigrafe.descrizione: An incomplete silver Roman finger ring only the bezel and shoulders now survive, the rest of the hoop is missing due to old breaks. The bezel is oval in shape and slightly raised and has five vertical lines across it which may represent an inscription. The shoulders are angular and triangular in shape with border grooves. Dimensions: bezel 9.87 by 8.41mm in size, width including shoulders is 15.93mm, 1.65g in weight. Discussion: This finger ring is most likely to be of Henig Type VIII (M Henig and J Ogden Antiquaries Journal 67 1987pp. 366-7, fig 2b), and as such probably dates to the 3 rd century. There is a similar shaped inscribed finger ring from Fillingham, Lincolnshire (2003 T259)…

epigrafe.descrizione: Six Roman silver denarii fused together and badly damaged in places. The coins are positioned so that they overlap slightly with one near the centre protruding slightly further out. An obverse is visible on each outer coin and have been identified as follows. Denarius of Hadrian [..] IAN[HA]DRIANVSAVG 117-138. Denarius of Trajan (prob ), no inscription showing, badly. damaged on right hand side. Reverse shows N?VN 98-117. The central coin shows the partial inscription [..] HADRIAN[VS]. Reverse type standing female with cornucopia, partial inscription COS. As these are the only datable components they provide a probable date range of 98-138

epigrafe.provenienza: contea di ritrovamento: Wiltshire (Inghilterra e Galles)
epigrafe.descrizione: A complete copper alloy Roman nummus of Emperor Constantine I (306-337 AD). Minted in Trier (326 AD). Obv. Laureate head facing right; legend: [CONSTAN]TINUS AUG. Rev. Camp gate with two turrets, no doors, star above; legend: PROVIDEN[TIAE AUGG]. Reece Period 16; RIC Vol VII, p209, No. 475

epigrafe.descrizione: A copper-alloy Roman Q-Radiate of the Emperor Allectus, dating to the period AD 293-296 (Reece Period 14) VIRTVS AVG reverse type depicting a galley right with mast, cabin and at least two rowers; waves. The obverse legend might be IMP C ALLECTVS P F I AVG which is not published for London Mint. London Mint. RIC V, pt 2 -. This coin is included in Sam Moorhead's corpus for RIC
epigrafe.fotografo: Salisbury and South Wiltshire Museum, Richard Henry
